forecasts.line: Kurzweil estimates a thousand dollars will buy enough computing to replay all human thought of ten millennia in microseconds by 2080.

works.author: Ray Kurzweil
works.title: The Singularity Is Near: When Humans Transcend Biology

ideas.author: Robert Heinlein
ideas.line: A dealership on the Moon that resells second-hand spaceships.
ideas.name: Lunar Used Spacecraft Lot
ideas.profit: not judged (not a technology, not something sold, not physically possible, or unclear)

verdict.money_why: Small operators buy the ships, and anyone with a patch of ground could open such a yard, so no seller keeps much.
verdict.prize_why: A yard that resells old ships is an ordinary trade, a convenience for buyers.

ideas.author: Robert Heinlein
ideas.line: A powerful engine that moves ships quickly between the planets of our solar system.
ideas.name: Lyle Drive
ideas.profit: a fat profit, kept by the maker

verdict.money_why: An engine is bought by whoever runs the ship, assumed here to be carriers, and established engine builders could copy it once it worked.
verdict.prize_why: An engine that moves ships faster or more cheaply would change the cost of all space transport.

ideas.author: Arthur C. Clarke
ideas.line: A cable tower linking the equator to a satellite far overhead for cheap access to orbit.
ideas.name: Space Elevator (Orbital Tower)
ideas.profit: a fat profit, kept by the maker

verdict.money_why: Shippers pay to send cargo up, and since another could be built once the idea was shown to work, the gain is assumed to go to the large builders and the holders of the few good ground sites.
verdict.prize_why: A fixed way up from the ground to the edge of space would slash the cost of reaching orbit for every firm that uses it.

ideas.author: Robert Heinlein
ideas.line: Another name for a cable tower lifting cargo from the ground to orbit.
ideas.name: Beanstalk
ideas.profit: a fat profit, kept by the maker

verdict.money_why: Shippers pay to send cargo up, and since another line could be built once the first was shown to work, the gain is assumed to go to the large builders and the holders of the few good ground sites.
verdict.prize_why: A lift from the ground to orbit would slash the cost of reaching space for every firm that uses it.

ideas.author: William Shatner
ideas.line: A jail housed on a station circling the planet.
ideas.name: Orbiting Penal Colony
ideas.profit: not judged (not a technology, not something sold, not physically possible, or unclear)

verdict.money_why: Only a government runs prisons, and the contractors that already build and supply them would be paid.
verdict.prize_why: A jail in orbit is a costly way to do what prisons on the ground already do.

ideas.author: Thomas A. Easton
ideas.line: Display panels grown from engineered plants with flat, leaf-like surfaces.
ideas.name: Leaf Screens
ideas.profit: competed away to users

verdict.money_why: People buy the panels for their homes, and since living stock multiplies once any of it is sold, no originator can hold it, so the growers and screen sellers that already hold stock and shops collect.
verdict.prize_why: A thin screen grown like a leaf could replace much printing and most rigid screens.

ideas.author: Philip K. Dick
ideas.line: A slang word for a manufactured humanlike being.
ideas.name: Andy
ideas.profit: not judged (not a technology, not something sold, not physically possible, or unclear)

verdict.money_why: Firms buy them as labour, and since many could build such bodies once shown how, the large manufacturers with factories and service networks collect what is left.
verdict.prize_why: This is only a slang word, so it is judged as the thing it names, assumed to be a humanlike machine that could do most human work.

ideas.work: Do Androids Dream of Electric Sheep?

ideas.author: Philip K. Dick
ideas.line: A manufactured being built to resemble and work like a human.
ideas.name: Replicant
ideas.profit: a moderate profit, kept by the maker

verdict.money_why: Firms buy them as labour, and since many could build such bodies once shown how, the large manufacturers with factories and service networks collect what is left.
verdict.prize_why: A manufactured being that works like a human could do most kinds of human work, which would change how most people work.

ideas.work: Do Androids Dream of Electric Sheep?

ideas.author: Murray Leinster
ideas.line: Large bears bred to be smarter so they can guard and befriend human explorers.
ideas.name: Mutated Kodiak Bears
ideas.profit: a fat profit, kept by incumbent firms

verdict.money_why: Exploring ventures pay, and because the bears breed, established animal breeders collect.
verdict.prize_why: Clever guard bears serve a narrow trade of explorers, unlike the pet dogs in this family.

ideas.author: Robert Heinlein
ideas.line: A dog bred through genetic engineering to be smarter and able to talk.
ideas.name: Neodog
ideas.profit: a fat profit, kept by licence holders

verdict.money_why: Owners pay, and because the dogs breed, established breeders collect instead of the originator.
verdict.prize_why: A talking, cleverer dog is a prized pet or working animal, which is a niche.

ideas.author: James Blish
ideas.line: Headgear that stimulates the brain to load knowledge straight into it.
ideas.name: Accelerated Schooling Helmet
ideas.profit: a fat profit, kept by licence holders

verdict.money_why: Families and learners would pay for it themselves, and once one firm had built the gear others could copy it and many could write the lessons, so no seller keeps much.
verdict.prize_why: Putting knowledge straight into the brain would replace years of schooling and training for most people.

ideas.author: George Alec Effinger
ideas.line: A plug-in brain cartridge that swaps in a chosen personality.
ideas.name: Moddy
ideas.profit: a fat profit, kept by incumbent firms

verdict.money_why: People would buy it for themselves, and since the method could be copied the owners of the stories, stars and channels people already follow would collect.
verdict.prize_why: Trying on a chosen personality would be an industry of its own, part entertainment and part borrowed skill.

ideas.author: John Barnes
ideas.line: A medium that lets people feel someone else's conscious experience directly.
ideas.name: XV
ideas.profit: a fat profit, kept by platforms

verdict.money_why: People would buy it for themselves, and since the method could be copied the owners of the stories, stars and channels people already follow would collect.
verdict.prize_why: Feeling another person's experience directly would be an entertainment and news industry of its own.

ideas.author: Neal Stephenson
ideas.line: Microscopic smart bricks that assemble themselves into structures.
ideas.name: Lithocule
ideas.profit: a moderate profit, kept by the maker

verdict.money_why: Builders buy them, and once they can be copied the established makers of building materials collect.
verdict.prize_why: Tiny bricks that build structures by themselves would change the cost of construction.

ideas.author: Yoshiyuki Tomino
ideas.line: A limbed combat spacecraft carrying heavy weaponry.
ideas.name: Mobile Armor
ideas.profit: a fat profit, kept by the maker

verdict.money_why: Armies pay, and only the heavy arms builders with yards, factories and contracts could turn them out, though any of them could.
verdict.prize_why: A piloted armoured war machine of that size would be a new class of weapon on the scale of tanks or warplanes.

ideas.author: Neal Stephenson
ideas.line: Fictional microscopic projectile machines used in combat in the story.
ideas.name: Ballisticules
ideas.profit: a fat profit, kept by incumbent firms

verdict.money_why: Armies would pay, and being hard to make does not stop others copying it once one maker has shown the way, so the established arms suppliers collect.
verdict.prize_why: Machines too small to see that are fired in combat are one more kind of ammunition, a narrow use.

ideas.author: Neal Stephenson
ideas.line: A fictional microscopic weapon used for assassination in the story.
ideas.name: Cookie-Cutters
ideas.profit: a fat profit, kept by incumbent firms

verdict.money_why: Secret services pay, and being strange does not make it hard to copy, so once one is built the arms makers that already supply them can make it too and collect.
verdict.prize_why: A weapon too small to see is a specialist tool for killing chosen people, a narrow use.

ideas.author: Neal Stephenson
ideas.line: A fictional cloud of tiny defensive machines shielding people from hostile airborne devices.
ideas.name: Immunocules
ideas.profit: a fat profit, kept by incumbent firms

verdict.money_why: Governments pay because no one can be charged one by one for clean air, and being hard to design does not stop others copying the machines once they exist, so the established defence suppliers collect.
verdict.prize_why: A cloud of tiny guardians against hostile airborne machines would be a basic public defence in a world that has such threats.

ideas.author: Jack Vance
ideas.line: Living trees that guard a boundary and let through only people carrying the correct signal.
ideas.name: Sentry Trees
ideas.profit: competed away to users

verdict.money_why: Assumes landowners and firms buy it; once such trees exist others could grow them, so no seller keeps much.
verdict.prize_why: A living fence that lets through only those with the correct signal is a kind of lock for a boundary.

ideas.author: Larry Niven
ideas.line: A spray-on communications film that sees, hears, zooms and projects images.
ideas.name: Webeye
ideas.profit: competed away to users

verdict.money_why: Nothing says it watches people, so firms are assumed to be the main buyers, and once made others could copy the film so no seller keeps much.
verdict.prize_why: A film sprayed on any surface that sees, hears and shows pictures would put cameras and screens anywhere.

ideas.author: Neal Stephenson
ideas.line: An engineered reef that draws in seawater to supply big coastal settlements.
ideas.name: Smartcoral Reef
ideas.profit: not judged (not a technology, not something sold, not physically possible, or unclear)

verdict.money_why: A government pays for the water supply of its coast, and since living stock multiplies once any of it is sold, no originator can hold it, so the marine builders and growers that already hold such public works contracts collect.
verdict.prize_why: A reef that draws in the sea to supply big coastal settlements would be a water business of its own.
